target_customer: Solar and energy EPC contractors, later multi-trade roofers and residential and commercial installers
problem: Solar contractors run projects on Salesforce, spreadsheets and paper, which inflates soft costs and delays installs.
business_model: B2B vertical SaaS subscription, with service-call and hardware OEM integrations
product_category: Workflow and operations software for solar and energy contractors

founders.name: Abdullah Al Zandani
education: B.S. Energy Engineering, 'Cal' 2021 (school as written on the YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page: worked at two unnamed solar companies in sales then operations, and as an energy efficiency building auditor at ADM.

founders.name: Max Kazakov
education: UC Berkeley, computer science and philosophy
founders.background_notes: YC page lists software, data and UX/UI skills.

technical_complexity.rationale: Vertical workflow CRM and project management with hardware OEM integrations (Enphase, SolarEdge) is standard SaaS engineering with some integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Industry-specific workflows and OEM integrations create some lock-in, but horizontal CRMs and solar tools can adapt.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: CB Insights lists Enerflo, Aurora and others as peers; those listings are undated and no source shows any copying or buying Coperniq.

market_need_then: The founders' launch pitch said soft costs were 17% of installation cost and that contractors used Salesforce and spreadsheets; this is company data, not independently verified.

identity.voice_and_tone: Casual and friendly in 2023 (sun and sunglasses emoji in the one-liner); the current site is operational and multi-trade focused.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive coined name, but no press about the brand itself was found and the name does not signal roofing or multi-trade.

pivots.from: Workflow software for solar and energy contractors
pivots.to: Operations software for multi-trade roofers with AI agents
pivots.why: The current site targets roofers and multiple trades; no source states the date or reason.

outcome_analysis: Coperniq raised a $4M seed led by Initialized Capital in November 2023, shortly after the Winter 2023 batch, and is still active. Its current site has widened from solar to multi-trade roofing with AI agents, which may reflect a weak solar market, but no source states that. No Series A, acquisition or shutdown was found.
notes: Seed confirmed by the YC page citing TechCrunch (Nov 6, 2023) and techstartups.com. Some aggregators say $4.5M total over 2 rounds; the extra $0.5M is unverified. Competitors left empty: peer listings are undated. Founder education 'Cal' as written; school not named in the YC bio beyond that.
